topic.subject: social
topic.title: Drainage: rivers of India
topic.scope: Himalayan and peninsular rivers, drainage basins, Ganga and Brahmaputra systems, lakes, river pollution

misconceptions.statement: A river basin is just the main river channel itself.
misconceptions.why: Students often visualize a river as a single line on a map rather than a catchment area.
misconceptions.fix: A river basin includes the main river and all its tributaries that collect water from a specific area.

probe.question: If a small stream flows into a tributary of the Ganga, is it part of the Ganga basin?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because it is not the Ganga river itself.

misconceptions.statement: All rivers in India originate from the Himalayas.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks often focus heavily on the Ganga and Indus systems, leading to an overgeneralization.
misconceptions.fix: Many major rivers in India, such as the Godavari and Krishna, originate from the Western Ghats in the peninsula.

probe.question: Where does the Godavari river originate?
probe.wrong_answer: It must start in the Himalayas because all big Indian rivers start there.

misconceptions.statement: Peninsular rivers are always dry because they do not have snow.
misconceptions.fix: Peninsular rivers are seasonal, meaning they have less water in the dry season but are not dry year-round.

probe.question: Do peninsular rivers have water during the monsoon season?
probe.wrong_answer: No, they are dry because they lack glaciers.

misconceptions.statement: River pollution is only caused by industrial waste.
misconceptions.why: Media campaigns often highlight industrial effluents, ignoring domestic and agricultural sources.
misconceptions.fix: Pollution is also caused by domestic sewage, agricultural runoff, and religious offerings.
